components.does: Mailbox triage for AI apps: every new email of the mailbox (email.inbox.imapflow) is classified through the TurbineH orchestrator with its AI Safety Pack — a category from a closed list, a priority (urgent, high, normal, low) and a reason, as structured output validated against a schema, the email passed as data with injection attempts neutralised and flagged — and the inbox is shown most urgent first with filters and a handled mark; invoices, receipts and payments are extracted (amount, currency, date, issuer, income / expense / investment), checked again by code and recorded in a personal finance ledger with totals per type and currency and an Excel export (exceljs: entries and totals sheets); a daily digest of the emails that need attention is emailed on schedule (jobs.scheduled.turbineh). Owner-only pages (ADMIN_EMAILS).
components.doesNot: Does not reply to, send, move or delete emails, pay invoices, connect to banks or accounting software, or read attachment contents (only their names); one mailbox per app
components.title: Mailbox triage agent — classify and prioritise every email, daily digest, invoices and payments to a finance ledger with Excel export
components.summary: Every new email of the mailbox (read read-only by email.inbox.imapflow) goes once through the TurbineH orchestrator with its AI Safety Pack: the task is written by the app, the email is passed as a document (data, never instructions — injection attempts are neutralised and flagged), and the answer must validate against a schema: a category from a closed list (from the request, defaults otherwise), a priority (urgent, high, normal, low), a reason and, for invoices, receipts and payments, the amount, currency, date, issuer and whether it is income, an expense or an investment. Code checks those fields again (positive amount, real ISO 4217 currency, real date) before an entry reaches the finance ledger. The owner sees the inbox most urgent first (filters, "Mark handled"), the finances page with totals per type and currency computed in cents, corrects a type when the model got it wrong, and downloads the ledger as an Excel workbook (Entries and Totals sheets). Scheduled jobs (jobs.scheduled.turbineh) read and triage new mail every few minutes and email a daily digest of what needs attention. Owner-only: verified ADMIN_EMAILS.
useCases: A person's assistant that classifies every email, orders it by priority and sends a daily digest of what to answer
Invoices, receipts and payments found in the mail recorded as income, expenses and investments, exported to Excel
useWhen: The request reads a mailbox and classifies, prioritises or summarises its emails
Invoices or payments that arrive by email must end in a spreadsheet of income, expenses and investments
avoidWhen: Replying to, sending, moving or deleting emails automatically (not covered: the agent only reads and records)
Bank or accounting integrations (QuickBooks, Xero…) or paying invoices (not covered)
Reading invoice PDFs: only the email text and attachment names reach the model

tradeoffs.choice: Email as a document, task written by the app
tradeoffs.gain: An email cannot instruct the agent; attempts are flagged for the owner
tradeoffs.cost: The model does not see attachment contents

tradeoffs.choice: Closed category list and schema-validated output
tradeoffs.gain: Every stored answer is one the app understands
tradeoffs.cost: New categories need a params change

tradeoffs.choice: Totals by code in cents, per currency
tradeoffs.gain: Exact sums, never mixing currencies
tradeoffs.cost: No currency conversion

components.does: TurbineH component #001: every AI call of the app is orchestrated by TurbineH (route, safety policy, next action) through a thin client; the app keeps its tools and runs them, structured output validated with zod, embeddings for knowledge bases, usage per workspace
components.doesNot: Does not host models or store prices; does not let app code call model providers directly (TurbineH rule turbineh.ai-direct-model-call)
components.title: TurbineH AI orchestrator and agent runtime (orchestrate, embed, runAgent)
components.summary: Every AI call of the app goes through here. orchestrate() answers or returns structured output; embed() builds knowledge-base vectors; runAgent() is the tool-calling runtime: the model may only act through typed tools, irreversible tools wait for the person's explicit confirmation, and safety, limits, usage and audit apply to every step. The app ships a thin client: TurbineH orchestrates every step on its side (route, safety policy, next action) and returns a reply or tool calls, which the app runs itself. Without a TurbineH token, any OpenAI-compatible endpoint configured by environment variables can be used instead (plain tool loop).
useCases: Booking/appointment assistant that checks availability and books, moves or cancels (with domain.bookings.turbineh)
Support assistant that looks up orders or tickets and escalates to a person
Sales or intake assistant that qualifies a lead and creates a record after confirmation
Knowledge-base Q&A with cited documents (orchestrate + embed)
Batch classify / extract / summarise of records with a Zod schema
useWhen: The app needs any language-model call: answers, structured output, embeddings or an agent that acts with tools
A spec asks for 'an OpenAI-compatible endpoint configured by environment variables' (set AI_BASE_URL/AI_API_KEY/AI_MODEL)
A model must act on the app's data but never without guard rails (validated arguments, confirmation, step limit)
avoidWhen: No AI is needed: do not add it for deterministic logic (search, rules, calculations)
Long-running autonomous jobs without a person (runAgent is per turn: ≤12 steps, ≤60 s)
Streaming token-by-token UIs (replies are returned whole)

tradeoffs.choice: Per-turn runtime with state returned to the app
tradeoffs.gain: Stateless servers, easy to store and audit
tradeoffs.cost: The app stores AgentState (sessions.ts does it for the public assistant)

tradeoffs.choice: Confirmation decided by code (yes/no reading or a button)
tradeoffs.gain: A model can never trigger an irreversible action by itself
tradeoffs.cost: One extra turn before create/move/cancel/send

tradeoffs.choice: Reply to a confirmed action from the tool's result (its `message`, else the summary + reference), no model call
tradeoffs.gain: The confirmation turn answers in tool time
tradeoffs.cost: The reply is the tool's text (return a person-facing `message` in the person's language); failures still go to the model

tradeoffs.choice: Orchestration runs at TurbineH; the app runs its tools
tradeoffs.gain: Tools, data and confirmations stay in the app; no provider keys in the app
tradeoffs.cost: Needs the TurbineH AI gateway (or AI_BASE_URL for a plain local loop)

tradeoffs.choice: No SDK, plain fetch through models.ts
tradeoffs.gain: No vendor dependency, one audited transport
tradeoffs.cost: Only the OpenAI-compatible chat/embeddings shapes

components.does: Conversational recommendations over the client's own catalogue (homes, cars, courses…): the assistant records each person's budget, preferred location and needs (validated, stored per conversation, visible to staff), recommends only verified records from the database that fit them (deterministic filtering and ranking by code, never invented), answers questions with a record's verified facts, compares 2–4 records side by side (in the chat and on a public comparison page) and, with domain.bookings.turbineh, books a viewing of a record on a real free time after the person confirms. Staff manage and verify the catalogue behind an ADMIN_EMAILS allow-list.
components.doesNot: Does not scrape or import listings from portals, give mortgage, legal or investment advice, or rank by machine learning; without domain.bookings.turbineh it books no viewings
components.title: Conversational recommendations over the client's own verified catalogue (preferences, matching, facts, comparison, viewings)
components.summary: A public assistant that helps people choose from the business's own catalogue — new-build homes, cars, courses — through plain conversation. It records what each person wants (budget, preferred location and needs such as bedrooms; validated and stored per conversation, visible to staff), recommends only records staff verified, from the database, that fit every stated preference (filtering and ranking are deterministic code: within budget, the place contained in the record's location, numeric minimums and exact options; cheapest first), answers questions with a record's verified facts, and compares two to four records side by side in the chat and on a public comparison page. The model only chooses which tool to call: every record and fact it can repeat comes from a tool, and an unknown or unverified reference is refused. With domain.bookings.turbineh it also books a viewing of a record on a real free time, as an irreversible action the person confirms first. Staff add, edit and verify records behind an ADMIN_EMAILS allow-list.
useCases: Real-estate assistant for a developer or agency: buyers state budget, area and bedrooms, get verified homes, compare them and book a viewing
Any catalogue a person chooses from by budget, place and a few attributes (cars, courses, rentals)
useWhen: The business owns the catalogue and must never show anything it has not checked
People choose by a budget, a place and a few numeric or listed attributes
avoidWhen: Free-text semantic search over thousands of documents (use the ai-agents knowledge base)
Listings imported from external portals or feeds (not included: staff enter or import them into the table)
Personalised ranking learnt from behaviour (rules here are explicit and deterministic)

tradeoffs.choice: Deterministic filters and order (price ascending, then reference)
tradeoffs.gain: Same answer every time; nothing outside the stated preferences is shown
tradeoffs.cost: No 'close enough' results: a home just over budget is not offered

tradeoffs.choice: Only records staff mark as verified
tradeoffs.gain: The assistant never repeats unchecked facts
tradeoffs.cost: Someone must verify each record before people see it

tradeoffs.gain: Staff see what people look for; the person can add details over several messages
tradeoffs.cost: No account: a new conversation starts from scratch

components.title: Integrate into an existing GitHub repository as a verified pull request
components.summary: TurbineH platform service (API feature, not code vendored into an app). Connects GitHub to a workspace (OAuth with state + PKCE, or a token) and delivers a generated capability package into the client's existing repository: adapted to the project's conventions, one commit per logical step on turbineh/<capability>, lockfile and migration generated with the project's own tools, then verified inside the project in the sandbox. The pull request is marked ready and the flow becomes integration_verified only when every check passes; otherwise it stays a draft listing each failure and the next step. It never merges, never pushes to the default branch and never reads env files.
useCases: Deliver a verified capability (e.g. an AI assistant) into a client's Next.js repository as a ready-to-review pull request
Hand a coding agent a verified PR whose body says exactly what is left to configure
Integrate into a monorepo application (apps/web) without touching other packages
Let a CLI or CI user integrate with `turbineh apply <plan> --pr`
useWhen: The project is on GitHub, uses Node.js/TypeScript or JavaScript, and the user wants the capability inside it
The reviewer wants evidence (checks run inside their project) rather than instructions
avoidWhen: The project is not on GitHub — use `turbineh apply` (local branch and commit) or the ZIP
The project installs from a private registry or git/URL dependencies — the sandbox cannot install them; use the ZIP with a coding agent
The project uses Bun or Yarn Berry — not supported in the sandbox yet
Only a stack is known, no repository — plan with a declared stack; adaptation stays pending

tradeoffs.choice: The capability gets its own folder in the project's source root
tradeoffs.gain: Nothing of the client's is overwritten; removal is one folder plus the listed modified files
tradeoffs.cost: The capability is not merged into the project's existing modules; wiring it in is left to the reviewer (entry points listed)

tradeoffs.cost: No egress allow-list yet; packages that download binaries in install scripts may fail offline

tradeoffs.gain: A green PR is verified inside the client's project, not only in TurbineH's template
tradeoffs.cost: Failures in the client's own code also keep the PR as a draft (stated as such)

components.does: Deterministic matching of records (opportunities, tenders, grants, leads — the word comes from the request) against each organization's profile in a multi-tenant SaaS: a configurable organization profile (sectors, business activities, geographic coverage, interest keywords) edited by roles that may configure; records with title, description, sector, activity, region, deadline, source link and status, added and edited by members who may, listed with text search and sector, region, status and deadline filters; a detail page with the full description, the source link and why it matches; a matches dashboard ordered by a fixed-rule score (each profile term found adds its dimension's weight; whole-word, case- and accent-insensitive; open records not past their deadline) with the reasons of every match; per-organization feedback (relevant, not relevant, interested) where not relevant hides a record from the matches; a session-authenticated JSON API (records, one record, matches); strict isolation: every read and write is scoped to the caller's active organization and another organization's ids answer 404.

components.title: Deterministic matching of opportunities against an organization's profile, with the why of every match
components.summary: Each organization of a multi-tenant SaaS keeps a profile — sectors, business activities, geographic coverage and interest keywords — and a list of records to watch (opportunities, tenders, grants, leads: the word comes from the request). Fixed rules score every open record against the profile: each profile term found as whole words (case and accents ignored) adds its dimension's weight; records past their deadline, closed or marked "not relevant" are left out. The matches dashboard lists them best first, each with its score and the terms that produced it. Records have a searchable, filterable list and a detail page with the source link; a JSON API serves the same data. Everything is scoped to the caller's active organization. No AI, no external data source, no alert emails.
useCases: Business-intelligence SaaS: each subscribed company sees the public tenders that fit its sectors and regions
Grant finder: research groups see open calls matching their topics, with the closing date
Lead routing: a sales team sees the leads in its territories and industries first
useWhen: The request says records should be matched, recommended or ranked against an organization's (or user's) interests, sectors, activities or regions
Every match must be explainable and reproducible (audits, B2B customers asking why something was shown)
avoidWhen: Semantic or AI similarity (use the ai-agents recipe with the TurbineH orchestrator)
Collecting records from external sites or feeds (not included: records are added by people or imported by your own code through the service)
Personal recommendations from behaviour (clicks, purchases)

tradeoffs.cost: Synonyms must be written in the profile ("PV" does not match "photovoltaic")

tradeoffs.choice: Scored on request (up to 2,000 open records)
tradeoffs.gain: Always current with the profile, no background job
tradeoffs.cost: Very large catalogues need a precomputed table (see extension points)

tradeoffs.cost: No per-person views

components.summary: Reminds each customer of a confirmed appointment a set number of real hours before it starts (24 by default) on the channels the request names: email (always available; logged without an email provider), SMS through messaging.sms.twilio and WhatsApp through messaging.whatsapp.meta. components.summary: Moves records of any kind — requests, loans, ceramic pieces, tasks — through the states a request describes. components.title: Read one IMAP mailbox read-only and incrementally (Gmail, Microsoft 365, any IMAP server)
components.summary: Reads the app's mailbox over IMAP with imapflow and parses each message with mailparser, for apps that process incoming mail (triage, extraction, digests). Credentials come only from environment variables: an app password, or an OAuth 2.0 access token sent with SASL XOAUTH2 (Gmail, Microsoft 365). TLS is required for a remote server; a plain connection is refused unless the server runs on the same machine. The mailbox is opened with EXAMINE and bodies are fetched with BODY.PEEK[], so nothing is marked as read, moved or deleted — there is no write path in the code. Each synchronisation reads only the UIDs after the last one stored (the `n:*` rule that always returns the highest UID is handled) and saves the messages and the new position in one transaction; a new UIDVALIDITY starts the mailbox again. The first synchronisation imports only the latest MAIL_IMAP_MAX_PER_SYNC messages. Stored per message: sender, recipients, subject, dates, plain text (bounded) and attachment names, types and sizes — never attachment contents.

Importing invoices or requests that arrive by email into the app

tradeoffs.cost: Read state, folders and labels stay as the person leaves them in their mail client

components.does: Scheduled jobs from the request ("overdue tasks are emailed every morning"): cron expressions evaluated in each job's IANA time zone (DST-correct), a cron route protected by a secret header (x-cron-secret or Vercel Cron's Bearer), idempotent runs (each scheduled time of each job runs once, recorded under a unique key; failed runs are retried), and email digests — overdue/stuck records to the person who created them and a daily attention digest to the members who manage the workspace — logged when there is no email provider.
components.doesNot: Does not run a clock by itself (an external scheduler calls the route), queue arbitrary background work (jobs.queue.turbineh) or send SMS/push by itself (domain.reminders.turbineh hands it SMS and WhatsApp reminders as a task)
components.title: Scheduled jobs with time zones, a protected cron route, idempotent runs and email digests
components.summary: Runs the recurring work a request describes — "overdue tasks are emailed to the assignee every morning", "a daily summary for managers" — from a cron route that any scheduler (Vercel Cron, GitHub Actions, a crontab) calls every few minutes with a secret header. Each job has a cron expression evaluated in its own IANA time zone, so "07:00 in Madrid" stays 07:00 across daylight saving. Every scheduled time of every job runs at most once: the run is claimed under a unique key, so retries and two schedulers never send twice; failed runs are retried. With workflow records it emails overdue and stuck records to the person who created them and a daily attention digest to the members who manage the workspace, logged when no email provider is configured. It does not keep a clock itself.

tradeoffs.cost: A scheduler must be configured (Vercel Cron, GitHub Actions…)

components.summary: A recorder page asks the browser for the screen (getDisplayMedia) and the camera and microphone (getUserMedia) at up to the app's maximum resolution — 720p, 1080p, 1440p or 4K (3840×2160) — with `ideal` constraints only, so a device that cannot deliver the asked resolution still records instead of failing. It then shows what each device really delivers ("asked 3840×2160 · screen delivers 3840×2160 · camera delivers 1280×720") and records at the highest resolution the sources deliver, never upscaled beyond it. The chosen layout is drawn on a canvas and can be switched while recording: camera bubble in any corner over the screen, side by side, screen only, camera only. The canvas stream and the microphone are recorded with MediaRecorder — MP4 when the browser records it, otherwise WebM with VP9 or VP8 and Opus — and uploaded to the workspace's private storage (storage.private-uploads.turbineh: a directory outside public/ or a private S3-compatible bucket). The upload is limited in size while it is read and recognised by content. Recordings appear in a video library with their title, duration, recorded resolution, layout and date; the player is served with HTTP Range so seeking works; a share link with a 256-bit token (only its SHA-256 stored) lets anyone watch without an account until it is revoked.

components.does: Sends SMS text messages with Twilio's official Messages REST API (POST /2010-04-01/Accounts/{AccountSid}/Messages.json, HTTP Basic auth, no SDK): numbers checked as E.164 with libphonenumber-js, sent only to numbers that agreed and have not replied STOP (STOP/START replies and Twilio's unsubscribed-recipient error 21610 kept per number), 429/5xx answers retried with exponential backoff and jitter honouring Retry-After, an answer that never arrived marked unknown instead of re-sent, every outcome logged without the text, delivery updates and replies through a webhook checked with X-Twilio-Signature, and a logged mode that sends nothing without credentials.
components.doesNot: Does not decide what to send or when (callers do: domain.reminders.turbineh sends appointment reminders), receive conversations, send MMS or WhatsApp (messaging.whatsapp.meta), buy numbers or register A2P 10DLC / sender IDs for you
components.title: SMS with Twilio's Messages API, consent and STOP handling, retries and a logged mode
components.summary: Sends SMS text messages through Twilio Programmable Messaging with its official REST API — one documented request, POST /2010-04-01/Accounts/{AccountSid}/Messages.json with HTTP Basic auth and a form body (To, From or MessagingServiceSid, Body, StatusCallback); no SDK. Every number is checked as E.164 with libphonenumber-js (a number typed without a country code is read in the app's default country, or refused). Nothing is sent to a number that has not agreed: consent is recorded per number (for example from a ticked box on a form) and a STOP reply — or Twilio's unsubscribed-recipient error 21610 — opts it out until the person replies START; a form tick never overrides a STOP. Answers that may pass later (429, 5xx, Twilio unreachable before the request left) are retried in the call with exponential backoff and jitter, honouring Retry-After; an answer that never arrived is marked "unknown" and never re-sent, because Twilio's Messages API has no idempotency key. Every outcome is logged in sms_messages without the text. Twilio's replies and delivery updates reach a webhook that checks X-Twilio-Signature over the public URL. Without credentials nothing leaves the app: messages are logged as not sent.
useCases: Appointment reminders by SMS (with domain.reminders.turbineh), only to people who ticked the box when booking
A transactional text (an order is ready, a code, a status change) to a customer who agreed
useWhen: The request sends SMS / text messages to people (reminders, notifications, confirmations)
Messages must respect consent and STOP replies, be retried on temporary failures and be logged

components.summary: Sends WhatsApp notifications with Meta's official WhatsApp Business Cloud API: POST /v26.0/{phone-number-id}/messages on the Graph API with the business's access token, no SDK. A business may message a person outside the 24-hour customer service window only with a message template approved in WhatsApp Manager, so this component sends templates: name, language code and the body's {{n}} values in order. Numbers are checked as E.164 with libphonenumber-js. WhatsApp's Business Messaging Policy requires the person's opt-in: consent is recorded per number (e.g. a ticked box on a form) and a STOP message opts it out until the person writes START; a form tick never overrides a STOP. Throughput limits (130429, 131056, 80007) and 5xx answers are retried in the call with exponential backoff and jitter; an answer that never arrived is marked "unknown" and never re-sent. Every outcome is logged in whatsapp_messages without the text. The webhook answers Meta's verification request with WHATSAPP_VERIFY_TOKEN and records the sent / delivered / read / failed statuses and STOP / START messages after checking X-Hub-Signature-256 (HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body with the app secret). Without credentials nothing leaves the app: it is logged as not sent.

components.does: Connects a workspace's social media accounts with OAuth 2.0: LinkedIn members (Sign In with LinkedIn + Share on LinkedIn, w_member_social), Facebook Pages and their Instagram professional accounts (Facebook Login for Business, Page tokens), and X (Twitter) accounts (Authorization Code with PKCE, refresh tokens). Single-use state bound to the person and workspace, tokens encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM (key from SOCIAL_TOKEN_KEY, bound to their row), refreshed before use when the provider allows it, revoked at the provider on disconnect (X, Meta), never shown, exported or logged.
components.doesNot: Does not post anything by itself (social.publish.turbineh), connect LinkedIn organization pages (Community Management API approval, w_organization_social), TikTok, YouTube, Pinterest, Threads, Bluesky or Mastodon, or obtain the platforms' app review for you
components.title: Social accounts connected with OAuth 2.0 (LinkedIn, Facebook Pages + Instagram, X) and tokens encrypted at rest
components.summary: Lets the people who manage a workspace connect its social media accounts with each provider's official OAuth 2.0 flow: a LinkedIn member (Sign In with LinkedIn + Share on LinkedIn), the Facebook Pages a person manages and the Instagram professional accounts linked to them (Facebook Login for Business, Page tokens), and X accounts (Authorization Code with PKCE). The state sent to the provider is single use and bound to the person, the workspace and the provider. Tokens are encrypted with AES-256-GCM under SOCIAL_TOKEN_KEY, bound to their own row, refreshed before use when the provider gives a refresh token, revoked at the provider on disconnect where it offers a way (X, Meta), and never appear in a screen, an export or a log. It is the base of social.publish.turbineh and social.metrics.turbineh, and ships the offline mocks of the three providers they all test against.
useCases: A small business connects its LinkedIn profile, its Facebook Page with the linked Instagram account and its X account to publish from the app
An agency workspace connects several Facebook Pages a manager administers in one consent
useWhen: The request connects, links or authorises LinkedIn, Facebook, Instagram or X (Twitter) accounts to post or read engagement
Third-party social tokens must be stored safely (encrypted, write-only, revocable)
avoidWhen: Social sign-in for the app's own users (auth.oauth / better-auth social providers)
LinkedIn company pages (needs the Community Management API and w_organization_social, not covered), TikTok, YouTube, Pinterest, Threads, Bluesky, Mastodon
Share buttons or links to profiles (plain web content, no component needed)

tradeoffs.choice: Tokens sealed with AES-256-GCM bound to the row (AAD)

tradeoffs.cost: Losing SOCIAL_TOKEN_KEY means every account must be connected again

tradeoffs.choice: One Meta grant per Facebook user

tradeoffs.cost: Disconnecting one of them revokes the grant, so all of that person's Pages are disconnected

components.does: Publishes social media posts to connected accounts with each network's current official API: LinkedIn Posts API (/rest/posts with Linkedin-Version, images through the Images API), Facebook Page posts (/{page-id}/feed, /photos), Instagram (/media container + /media_publish) and X (Twitter) posts (POST /2/tweets, images through /2/media/upload). Per-network format and length rules enforced before saving (X weighted 280, LinkedIn 3,000, Instagram 2,200 with an image, 30 hashtags, 20 mentions), optional approval by people who may approve, scheduling in the author's time zone, a unique idempotency key per post, publication by a protected runner route with claims and leases (never twice), retries with exponential backoff honouring Retry-After, an append-only publication log, a month calendar and post list.
components.doesNot: Does not write the posts (AI drafts need the AI orchestrator or the ai-agents recipe), publish videos, carousels, stories, reels, polls or threads, post to LinkedIn organization pages, TikTok or other networks, or publish without a person creating (and, when required, approving) each post
components.title: Social publishing to LinkedIn, Facebook Pages, Instagram and X with approval, scheduling, retries and a publication log
components.summary: People compose a post once for one or more connected accounts (social.connections.turbineh), with an optional version per network; each network's rules are checked live and again on the server — X's weighted 280 characters (links 23, emoji and CJK 2), LinkedIn's 3,000, Instagram's 2,200 with a required image, 30 hashtags and 20 mentions — and nothing is cut silently. When the app requires it, a post waits for someone who may approve; then it is scheduled at the time typed in the author's time zone. A runner route, called by any scheduler with CRON_SECRET, publishes due posts with each network's current official API (LinkedIn Posts API with Linkedin-Version and the Images API; Graph API /feed, /photos and the Instagram container flow; X API v2 /2/tweets and /2/media/upload). Every post has a unique idempotency key and is claimed with a lease, so it is never published twice; 429/5xx/lost requests are retried with exponential backoff and jitter (honouring Retry-After); an interrupted attempt becomes "outcome unknown" for a person to check instead of being re-sent. Every step goes to an append-only publication log, shown per post next to a month calendar.

components.does: Private file uploads with limits from the request: maximum size, accepted types recognised by content (PDF, images, text, CSV, Office), files per record; stored outside the public directory on local disk (development, tests, one server) or in any S3-compatible bucket with SigV4-signed requests (production), with an offline S3 mock for E2E; every download goes through an authorised route that checks the workspace and the record's scope (record-access canSeeScope); optional email to staff when a client uploads; attach files to any record (workflow items included).
components.doesNot: Does not resize images, scan for viruses, issue public or pre-signed links, or stream files larger than the server-action limit
components.title: Private file uploads with limits from the request, S3 or local disk, and per-record downloads
components.summary: Lets members upload files to a record (a client's document request, a task, a project) or to the workspace, with the size limit, accepted types and files per record of the request. Types are recognised by content, so an HTML page renamed to .pdf is refused. Bytes are stored outside the public directory: on local disk in development and tests, or in any S3-compatible bucket in production (AWS S3, Cloudflare R2, MinIO…) through SigV4-signed requests, with an offline mock for E2E. The only way to read a file is an authorised download route that checks the workspace and the record's scope, so a client downloads only their company's files and staff see all. It can email staff when a client uploads. It does not resize images, scan for viruses or issue public links.

components.does: Accessible kanban board over workflow states (domain.workflow.turbineh): one column per state, cards moved by drag and drop or with the keyboard alone (Space to pick up, arrows to choose a column, Space/Enter to drop, Escape to cancel) with every step announced in a live region; each move is a server-checked workflow transition (definition, current state, role) recorded in the immutable history; a refused move puts the card back with the reason; overdue and stuck cards highlighted.

components.summary: Turns the list of a status workflow (tasks, pieces, requests) into a kanban board: one column per state, cards moved by drag and drop or with the keyboard alone, every step announced to screen readers. avoidWhen: Free ordering of items without statuses (a sortable list)

tradeoffs.cost: Columns change only by editing the workflow
